thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoint /v1/stream in us-west-2. p95=850ms, p99=4.2s over last 5m. Error rate low, but many streaming stalls reported. Automated reroute attempted to fallback pool, 12% of requests saw retries.

maria: I'm on call. pulling logs now — starting triage.

ashwin: seeing repeated correctable ECC logs on gpu-node-17 (nvml reports ECC_Corrected=continuous). thermal sensors on the node show GPU5 temps oscillating and then throttle events. suspect hardware-level throttling causing stalls in KV cache fetches.

olivia: confirming hardware: "GPU5 ECC corrected errors spike at 16:02 UTC, thermal throttle at 16:04 UTC" — node metrics: fan speed 70%, package temp hit 92C -> GPU driver triggered throttle.

maria: quick mitigation plan: 1) isolate gpu-node-17 (drain new work), 2) shift streaming traffic off to fallback pool (quantized v1-small) for 15m, 3) enable prefix-KV cache reuse aggressor on routers, 4) notify support + customers. doing steps 1-3 now.

paul: on the routing side I can open an emergency policy to drop heavy long-context requests to fallback. Preparing policy 'fallback-thermal-4167' — applying it in 10s.

jess: support triage — I'm pulling list of active customer sessions drawing from us-west-2 streaming. early look: 3 paid customers with >50 concurrent streaming sessions each, a few dev accounts. I'll DM affected CSMs. severity: SLO breach impacting a subset of sessions (partial degradation).

maria: command snippets for the mitigation I'm running:
```
# cordon and drain node
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
redwoodctl node drain gpu-node-17 --mode=graceful --timeout=5m

# routing change (applied via control plane)
redwoodctl routing apply --policy fallback-thermal-4167 --selector region=us-west-2 --force
```

ashwin: logs (excerpt):
```
[16:02:11] GPU5 ECC_CORRECTABLE error count +1
[16:03:42] nvml: GPU5 temperature 91.8C
[16:04:05] NVML_THERMAL_THROTTLING GPU5 -> reduced clocks
[16:04:12] streaming: p99 stall detected: stall_ms=3200 session_id=xyz
[16:04:15] KV cache miss spike on gpu-node-17
```

maria: drain in progress, 120 active streams to reschedule; control plane shows 98% success reroute so far. routing policy is in effect.

olivia: infra note — GPU5 has had intermittent ECC correctables in the past 72h but no unrecoverables. I've opened a hardware ticket with the provider (ticket# HW-93412). We can hot-swap or evict node after drain.

samir: I see p99 dropping now to ~600-900ms after fallback policy. p95 stable ~200-350ms. Still seeing occasional stalls tied to sessions already in-flight. Recommend increasing retry window on streaming client for the next 10m.

jess: CSMs notified. I've posted a short status to affected customers: "We're seeing transient streaming stalls in us-west-2 due to hardware throttling on a GPU node. We're rerouting traffic; you may see brief retries. We're monitoring and will update in 15 minutes."

maria: handing off to ashwin for deeper root cause & remediation. my todo: capture heap/kv cache state, save relevant traces, and start postmortem doc.

ashwin: taking over. immediate next steps: 1) full nvml dump from gpu-node-17, 2) run microbench on remaining GPUs to check for propagation, 3) verify quantization runtime isn't regressing accuracy for fallbacks.

ashwin: nvml dump attached to hardware ticket and to /incidents/4167890123/artifacts. also pushed a temporary autoscale bump for fallback pool +2 nodes to keep capacity while we evacuate.

paul: rollback plan if mitigation affects customer latency: we can re-route a % of traffic back to other healthy nodes in us-west-2 region (canary at 5% -> 20%). prefer to keep fallback until node replaced.

maria: customer impact summary for the timeline so far:
- window: 16:00-16:18 UTC
- cardinality: ~0.7% of global requests, 3 enterprise customers with partial streaming stalls
- severity: SLO breach at p99 for 18m, p95 unaffected beyond normal variability
- mitigation: routing fallback + node drain -> p99 improved to ~700ms after 6m

jess: logging incident impact in ops portal and flagging follow-up outreach for customers with SLA credits if root cause warrants.

olivia: hardware update: provider scheduled node replacement for 16:45 UTC. they recommend not rebooting in-place until replacement arrives because of intermittent ECC history.

ashwin: brief root-cause hypothesis: thermal cycling caused sustained ECC correctables on GPU5 which then triggered throttling; throttling reduced effective compute and introduced KV cache latency on that node causing streaming stalls. We'll confirm via nvml hist and kernel messages.

maria: postmortem owners: ashwin (technical lead), olivia (infra/hardware), jess (customer comms). I'll create the postmortem doc and run the timeline details. action items to include: node quarantine thresholds, faster automated routing when ECC correctables spike, and a runbook update for streaming stalls to prefer draining earlier.

samir: quick runbook note: add detection rule: if ECC_correctable_rate > 50/min AND thermal_throttle_count > 1 in 5m -> auto-evacuate node and route to fallback.

ashwin: will validate fallbacks didn't introduce logits/regression; so far sampling looks good. initiating longer eval on quantized v1-small for edge cases.

maria: thanks all. I'll monitor until replacement confirmed. if anything changes, update thread.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall (maria). Status: mitigated -> recovering. Postmortem pending.

jess: final note for handoff: I'll track any follow-up customer replies and escalate as needed.

ashwin: replacement completed at 16:48 UTC, node reimage not performed (provider swapped hardware). Monitoring metrics look normal, ECC counters stabilized. I'm leaving the routing policy enabled for 10m to be safe, then gradually remove.

maria: taking back oncall. closing active mitigation. thanks team.
